clue.text: Sticker on post from Eastern Europe

definitions.text: Sticker on post from Eastern Europe

parts.words: Sticker on post from Eastern Europe
parts.note: a sticker read as one who sticks people on posts: the Wallachian prince who skewered enemies on stakes

explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth-century Romanian ruler Vlad III was notorious for executing enemies by driving stakes through them.

clue.text: Playing unmusically, a quintet finally creates bedlam

indicators.note: playing the letters about, as a musician plays with notes, rearranges them
finally picks only the closing letter of quintet

explanation.surface: A five-piece band plays out of tune and the result is chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' looks like part of the musical picture but is the anagram signal: UNMUSICALLY, A and T (the last letter of quintet, from 'finally') are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, from London's Bethlem Hospital, was the byword for a madhouse, an old term for a mental institution.

clue.text: I may demand uniform of Engineers seized by Lewis and Morse perhaps

indicators.note: seized by says the engineers are held inside the detective, as a suspect is held

parts.note: Lewis, Morse's sidekick in the TV detective series, is a DS, a Detective Sergeant
RE is the Royal Engineers, so 'of Engineers' is the possessive RE'S
Morse is an example of a code

explanation.surface: The Engineers are arrested by the two Oxford TV detectives, who might insist on uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Engineers' is the possessive RE'S, held inside DS; 'Morse perhaps' is not the detective but the telegraph code.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule on what to wear at an event or workplace may require a set outfit.

clue.text: Creature in jeopardy hurtles skyward

indicators.note: skyward says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some animal in peril shoots up into the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the hidden run ARDYH across 'jeopardy hurtles'; in a down clue 'skyward' reads it upwards, giving the many-headed serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hydra was the many-headed serpent monster of Greek myth slain by Heracles.

clue.text: Where you'll find second of girlfriends has turned to the flesh

parts.words: Where you'll find second of girlfriends
parts.note: the second letter of girlfriends, I, is found in G-R, between its first and third letters
to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: A lover's second girlfriend has gone native, turning fleshly.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter has said 'has' should have read 'to have', to match OWN; the first part is a riddle: the letter I sits 'in GR' in girlfriends.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrown toenail has grown back into the surrounding skin.

clue.text: Survivor buried in a layer of stucco

indicators.note: buried in says one word is sunk inside another, as something buried lies within the ground

parts.note: a as in 'ten pounds a head' means per
a survivor is one who lasts, a laster

explanation.surface: Someone who came through is entombed in a coat of plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is the trick: it means 'per', as in 'twice a day'. 'buried in' sinks the survivor inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plasterer is the tradesman who spreads a coat of render or stucco on walls.

clue.text: Vigorously apply not cloth but shampoo, taking tips

parts.note: the cloth means the clergy, so not cloth is lay, of the laity

indicators.note: taking tips takes the end letters of but and shampoo

explanation.surface: Scrub hard, using shampoo rather than a flannel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cloth' is not a flannel but the clergy; 'tips' here are the final letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The old verb to lay to means to set to work energetically, as rowers lay to their oars.

clue.text: Abandon luxury? How horrible! I tuck into bunk

indicators.note: tuck into says these pieces are slipped inside another word, like bedclothes tucked into a bunk

parts.note: bunk means nonsense, rot
UGH is the exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from a grim cabin bed but climbs into it anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunk' looks like a bed but means nonsense; 'tuck into' slips the exclamation and I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rough it is to live without comforts, as campers do.

clue.text: Cook poorly, having shelled egg that should be beaten

parts.note: to underdo food is to cook it too little

indicators.note: shelled strips the outer letters off egg, as a shell comes off an egg

explanation.surface: A bad cook peels an egg that ought to have been whisked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' suggests whisking eggs, but the definition means the contestant expected to lose.
explanation.definitionFit: An underdog is the competitor expected to lose a contest.

clue.text: See 2
England rugby player's regretting miss

definitions.meaning: Chris Oti won thirteen England caps on the wing; with the apostrophe-s his name gives the letters
the title character of Cole Porter's song who 'regrets she's unable to lunch today'

explanation.surface: An England rugby international rues a missed kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' looks like a missed kick but is the title of the woman in Cole Porter's song.
explanation.definitionFit: Chris Oti was an England winger of the late 1980s, so the player's is OTI'S; and Cole Porter's song 'Miss Otis Regrets' names a lady who regrets.

clue.text: Something in grocer's upsetting to a shopper

indicators.note: upsetting knocks the letters over into a new order

explanation.surface: A shop sign's punctuation annoys a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'grocer's apostrophe' is the stray mark in signs like 'apple's 50p'; here it sits correctly in 'grocer's', which makes the definition doubly apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark showing possession sits in the word grocer's, and is famously misused by greengrocers.

clue.text: Parrot encountered on the way to India

definitions.meaning: to parrot is to repeat mechanically

definitions.text: encountered on the way to India
definitions.meaning: in the radio alphabet Delta, ..., Foxtrot, Golf, Hotel lead up to India

explanation.surface: A bird spotted during a journey to the subcontinent.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a trip east; the second half really means the call sign met before 'India' in the phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat what is heard, as a reverberation does; and in the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for E comes before that for I.

clue.text: Being big boy — and healthy — it should be eaten

parts.note: Gene is a boy's name

indicators.note: should be eaten says a word goes inside, swallowed by another

parts.note: rosy, as in rosy cheeks, means healthy

explanation.surface: A large lad who is fit ought to be devoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being big' looks like size; it means being big-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being big-hearted or magnanimous is liberality, a readiness to give.

clue.text: Target resort on King's epic journey

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort: sort the letters again into a new order

parts.note: re means on or about
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A holiday spot is targeted along a royal's legendary voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but is re-sort, the anagram signal for TARGET plus RE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Trek was the 1830s migration of Boer settlers into the South African interior.

clue.text: Item of furniture has piano covering area leading up to it

indicators.note: leading up to says the first piece comes before the next
covering says one piece wraps round another

parts.note: piano is the musical direction for soft
able means up to it, capable

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture has a piano over the spot just in front of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano' is the musical marking SOFT, which covers A; this leads up to ABLE, from 'it' as in being up to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa table is a long narrow table placed behind or beside a settee.

clue.text: I myself may attend thumb, at last

definitions.text: I myself may attend thumb, at last

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the setter is the crossword compiler referring to himself

explanation.surface: Someone offers to look after an injured thumb in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I myself' is a crossword convention: the compiler is the setter. The whole clue also describes someone who treats a broken digit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonesetter is a practitioner who resets fractured or dislocated joints, as a damaged digit might need.

clue.text: Pungent plea for one to hold forth

parts.note: 'Oh do!' is a pleading request to someone
to rant is to hold forth at length

explanation.surface: A strong-smelling request asks a person to speak at length.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'Oh do rant!', a plea for one to hold forth.
explanation.definitionFit: An odorant is a strong-smelling substance, so the word describes something pungent.

clue.text: Various go-karts no good: one's introduced chariots

indicators.note: introduced says a letter is brought inside
various means in assorted forms, so the letters are mixed
no says the following letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Assorted go-karts, none of them any good, have chariots brought in among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' scrambles GO-KARTS with G taken out ('no good'), giving TROKAS; 'introduced' slips I (one) in.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a Russian vehicle drawn by three horses abreast, a carriage like a chariot.

clue.text: Send off one involved in dangerous play

definitions.meaning: to send off can mean to dismiss from a job or to discharge a gun
the idiom 'playing with ...' means taking a dangerous risk

explanation.surface: A player is dismissed after a reckless challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send off' and 'play' suggest a red card on the pitch; the second half points to the idiom 'playing with fire'.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss someone or launch a missile is to discharge; and the flames are what you are 'playing with' when taking risks.

clue.text: One in olden times consumed by passion, the heart's prison?

indicators.note: consumed by says pieces are swallowed inside another word

parts.note: rage is a violent passion
I is the Roman numeral for one
BC marks dates before Christ, olden times

explanation.surface: Someone in the past is eaten up by passion, a heart imprisoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in olden times' reads as one person in the past but gives two pieces side by side; 'consumed by' puts both inside the passion word.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax's frame of bones encloses and protects the heart, so it can be pictured as its cell.

clue.text: Died apprehending Estonian, say, in search for weapon

indicators.note: in places the whole run inside another word

parts.note: to comb is to search thoroughly

indicators.note: apprehending means seizing, so one piece holds another

parts.note: OB, short for obiit, means died
an Estonian is an example of a Balt, from a Baltic state

explanation.surface: A dead man who arrested a Baltic national had been hunted for a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apprehending' puts the Baltic national inside the abbreviation for died; 'in' puts that inside the search word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobalt bomb is a hypothetical nuclear device designed to spread long-lasting radioactive fallout.

clue.text: Support one cheerful old man raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raised says the run is read upwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
up means cheerful, in high spirits
pa, the old man, means father

explanation.surface: A happy father is held up by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the whole run I + UP + PA, read upwards in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Appui is a word borrowed from French meaning a prop or point of support, as in a military defensive position.

clue.text: Painter's book covering unusually large children

indicators.note: in a down clue covering puts the first piece on top of the next

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, unusually large

explanation.surface: An artist's volume is bound over big kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually large' is OS, the clothing label for outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieronymus Bosch was the Dutch artist of The Garden of Earthly Delights.

clue.text: By overcoming bias, he's become more familiar

parts.note: the word 'by' takes the place of 'bias' at the end of a longer biblical name, so that name shrinks

explanation.surface: Someone shakes off prejudice and grows friendlier.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace BIAS with BY in TOBIAS: the result is that name's familiar short form.
explanation.definitionFit: The short form of the biblical name Tobias is a pet name, the more familiar version.

clue.text: One stony path actually leads up close to the castle

indicators.note: leads picks the first letters of path and actually
close to takes the last letter of the following word

parts.note: R is the chess notation for a rook, or castle

explanation.surface: A rocky track really climbs to near the fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stony' suggests the path; it means stony-broke. 'castle' is the chess piece, R.
explanation.definitionFit: Stony is short for stony-broke, penniless, so a destitute person is one.

clue.text: Rock group regularly in Caribbean's back from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue from the east means read right to left
regularly takes every other letter of these words

explanation.surface: A band plays now and then in the islands' hinterland, coming from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: Every second letter of 'in Caribbean's back' gives NAIBASAK, which 'from the east' reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Kasabian is an English indie band from Leicester.

clue.text: Half-inch objects collected by stupid idiot getting close

parts.note: thick means stupid

indicators.note: collected by says one piece is gathered inside another

parts.note: an ass is a fool
half-inch is rhyming slang for pinch, to steal, and to thieve is to steal objects

explanation.surface: Something stolen is picked up by a dim fool who comes near.
explanation.walkthrough: HALF-INCH is Cockney rhyming slang for pinch, steal; 'collected by' puts the stealing verb inside the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Being very close friends is described by the idiom about criminals sharing secrets.
